children: The steelmaker said the attacks caused fatalities, injuries and extensive damage to production facilities, with the latest strike taking place on 21 September. Five employees were killed across the four attacks and 17 were injured, including one who remains in a critical condition.
ArcelorMittal has told the Ukrainian government that operations cannot currently be resumed in a safe and sustainable manner.
It said it would instead focus on preserving the site’s infrastructure so that restarting production could remain an option once conditions improve.
"It is with deep regret that we have concluded that we are no longer able to safely operate ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih," said Mauro Longobardo, chief executive of ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih.

"We are discussing the future of the plant with the Government of Ukraine and will focus on preserving the infrastructure, so when peace finally returns, options for restarting production remain available.”
Since Russia’s invasion began in February 2022, ArcelorMittal has provided more than $700m of financial support to keep the Ukrainian business operating.
Despite the news on Friday, the Amsterdam-listed stock was 2.7% higher at €63.70 by 1031 BST.
